content.user_title: Build Azure Key Vault Certificate Workflows in Rust
content.value_statement: Azure certificate operations require correct SDK models, authentication, and policies. This skill provides focused Rust examples for common Azure Key Vault certificate workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to add the Azure certificate and identity crates to a Rust project.
Creates a CertificateClient with DeveloperToolsCredential and an Azure Key Vault endpoint.
Retrieves certificate metadata and formats an X.509 thumbprint.
Creates and imports certificates with Azure SDK request models.
Deletes certificates and streams certificate property listings.
Reads and updates certificate policies through the Rust SDK.
limitations: The snippets are partial examples and require application-specific error handling and project setup.
Execution requires an Azure vault, network access, valid Entra ID credentials, and suitable RBAC permissions.
The skill covers certificates, not Azure Key Vault secrets or cryptographic key workflows.
Recovery, purge, renewal automation, and expiration monitoring are described but not implemented.

use_cases.title: Add Certificate Access
use_cases.description: Set up authentication and retrieve certificate metadata from an existing Azure Key Vault.

use_cases.title: Manage Certificate Lifecycles
use_cases.description: Create, import, list, and delete certificates with policy-aware Rust SDK calls.

use_cases.title: Review Azure Certificate Code
use_cases.description: Check client setup, RBAC assumptions, certificate policies, and secret handling before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Connect to a Vault
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to connect a Rust application to Azure Key Vault Certificates using DeveloperToolsCredential and my vault URL.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve a Certificate
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Rust workflow that retrieves a named certificate and explains which returned fields contain public certificate data.

prompt_templates.title: Create and Import Certificates
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare certificate creation and PFX or PEM import in Rust. Include required models, secure password handling, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Lifecycle Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Rust certificate service using Azure Key Vault. Cover policies, listing, deletion, RBAC, expiration monitoring, retries, and production credential selection.

output_examples.input: Explain how my Rust service should authenticate to Azure Key Vault during development and production.
output_examples.output: Development uses DeveloperToolsCredential with an authorized local identity. Production should use an appropriate managed identity with the minimum certificate permissions.

output_examples.input: Summarize the steps for importing a password-protected certificate.
output: Load the encoded certificate and password from protected sources.
Build the import parameters without logging sensitive values.
Call the import operation and inspect the returned certificate metadata.
Clear temporary sensitive data when the application design permits.

output_examples.input: What should a certificate policy review cover?
output_examples.output: Review the issuer, subject, validity period, renewal behavior, key properties, deletion protection, and the RBAC permissions used by the application.

best_practices: Use managed identity in production and grant only the certificate permissions required by each workload.
Keep import passwords and certificate material outside source code, logs, and command history.
Test lifecycle operations in a non-production vault and monitor certificate expiration.
anti_patterns: Do not embed certificate passwords, private material, or production vault identifiers in source code.
Do not grant full certificate management rights to read-only workloads.
Do not assume partial snippets include production error handling, retries, auditing, or recovery.

faq.question: Which Rust crates does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses azure_security_keyvault_certificates for certificate operations and azure_identity for Entra ID authentication.

faq.question: Does the skill manage private keys directly?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on certificate operations exposed by Azure Key Vault Certificates and does not cover the separate key client.

faq.question: Can I use DeveloperToolsCredential in production?
faq.answer: It is intended for development scenarios. Use a production credential appropriate for your Azure hosting environment, usually managed identity.

faq.question: What permissions are required?
faq.answer: Permissions depend on the operation. Grant the minimum Azure RBAC role or custom permissions needed for reading, creating, importing, updating, or deleting certificates.

faq.question: Does deletion permanently remove a certificate?
faq.answer: The documented delete operation uses Azure Key Vault soft deletion. Permanent purge requires a separate operation and additional authorization.

faq.question: Are the examples complete applications?
faq.answer: No. They are focused snippets that require project setup, configuration, error handling, testing, and environment-specific security controls.
